plan.title: All About Me
plan.weeklyOverview: Preschoolers study identity through mirrors, names, chosen families, feelings art, and cooperative movement. We avoid body and family-size comparisons and celebrate many ways to look, move, and belong.
plan.objectives:
Develop self-awareness and confidence
Learn and recognize their names and letters in names
Explore body parts and facial features
Build emotional awareness and vocabulary
Strengthen communication skills
Celebrate similarities and differences among peers
plan.weeklyMaterials:
Child-safe mirrors
Preferred-name cards and chunky letters
Family photos or drawings
Skin-tone crayons
Paper and clipboards
Blocks and linking cubes
Scarves and ribbon
Picture card pack PDF
Stickers or paper dots
Play kitchen props
Emotion/interest cards
Folded blank books
plan.vocabularyWords:
me
name
family
friend
happy
sad
eyes
nose
hands
body
same
different
special
plan.familyConnection: Invite families to share photos and talk about family members. Encourage children to practice saying their names and identifying body parts at home.
plan.observationOpportunities: Observe self-recognition, emotional awareness, communication skills, social interactions, confidence, and participation.
plan.adaptations: Provide visual supports, family photos, and individualized assistance as needed. Encourage participation at each child's comfort level.

monday.theme: Mirrors, Names, and People We Love
monday.objectives:
Notice myself in a mirror.
Find my preferred name and first letter.
Share a photo or drawing of people who matter—without ranking families.
monday.materials:
Child-safe mirrors
Preferred-name cards
Chunky letters
Family photos or drawings
Clothespin gallery string
monday.vocabulary: me, name, family, friend, happy, sad
monday.circleTime: Sing I Am Me. Pass a mirror for a quick peek. Preview name trays.
monday.outdoorPlay: Chalk first letters on the sidewalk; match with leaf tokens.
monday.familyConnection: Invite a drawing or photo of people/pets who care for the child, plus preferred-name pronunciation.
monday.observations: Notes mirror avoidance supports; preferred-name accuracy.
monday.adaptations: Peek-a-boo before mirrors; photo+name for younger finders.

items.title: Mirror Me
items.objective: Notice my face in a mirror and copy a friend’s expression.
items.description: Mirror play that starts by copying the child before asking them to copy the teacher.
items.materials:
Child-safe mirrors or taped acrylic tiles
Picture cards of feelings (optional)
items.setup: Sit beside children at mirror height. Keep feeling cards face-down until engaged.
items.steps:
1. Copy the child’s expression first.
2. Invite them to copy yours.
3. Optional: peek at one feeling card.
4. End with a shared silly face.
items.teacherRole: Follow the child’s lead; never force eye contact.
items.teacherLanguage: I see your smile. Can you make my surprised face?
items.observationOpportunities:
Notices teacher’s matching face
Sustains an expression
Comfort with mirrors
items.extensions: Take turns being the face leader.
items.adaptations: Peek-a-boo with a scarf before mirror for mirror-averse children.
items.safetyNotes: Acrylic or metal mirrors only. Tape edges.
items.supportAdaptations: Teacher holds the mirror; child glances briefly.
items.additionalChallenge: Children lead a three-face sequence.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers join for peek games; preschoolers lead.
items.cleanupTip: Wipe mirrors after the group.

items.title: My Name Discovery
items.objective: Find my name card and match my first letter.
items.description: Preferred-name cards and chunky letters on a low tray.
items.materials:
Preferred-name cards
Chunky letter magnets or foam letters
Low tray
items.setup: Verify preferred names with families. Set three cards at a time.
items.steps:
1. Child finds their card among two others.
2. Match the first letter.
3. Say the name aloud with pride.
4. Store card in the name mailbox.
items.teacherRole: Honor nicknames families approve; no speed contests.
items.teacherLanguage: Which card is yours? What letter starts your name?
items.observationOpportunities:
Finds card among two others
Seeks first letter by shape or asking
items.extensions: Trace the first letter on a friend’s palm with permission.
items.adaptations: Partner hunt for letters.
items.safetyNotes: Letters large enough to fail choke test.
items.supportAdaptations: Only the child’s letter in the bowl at first.
items.additionalChallenge: Build more letters of the name.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Younger children match photo + name card.
items.cleanupTip: Name cards into labeled envelopes for Friday.

items.title: Family Photo Sharing
items.objective: Share people who matter using a photo or drawing—without explaining family structure.
items.description: Children point and name freely; drawings and picture cards are equal to photos.
items.materials:
Family photos or drawings
Clothespin string or board
Picture cards of caring roles
items.setup: Accept drawings. Privacy note posted. No required structure talk.
items.steps:
1. Child chooses what to share.
2. Points and names.
3. Peers listen.
4. Clip to the gallery string.
items.teacherRole: Never require explanations of who lives where.
items.teacherLanguage: Who would you like to show us? Tell us one thing you love doing together.
items.observationOpportunities:
Whom they name first
Interest in a peer’s photo
items.extensions: Sticky note with one dictated word.
items.adaptations: Teacher holds the photo while the child points.
items.safetyNotes: Respect privacy—no public posting without permission.
items.supportAdaptations: Picture cards if no photo/drawing yet.
items.additionalChallenge: Dictate a sentence for the gallery.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers point; preschoolers dictate captions.
items.cleanupTip: Return photos to labeled envelopes immediately.

monday.teacherPreparation: Confirm preferred names. Post privacy note. Stage mirrors at child height.
monday.activityFlow: Mirror Me → My Name Discovery → Family Photo Sharing.
monday.questions: What do you notice in the mirror? Which card is your name?
monday.observationFocus: Mirror comfort; name recognition; whom children choose to share.

tuesday.objectives:
Fill a personal belonging circle without comparing families.
Move with inclusive options.
Start process self-portraits.
tuesday.materials:
Circle papers
Dots/stickers
Caring-role cards
Skin-tone crayons
Open movement space
tuesday.vocabulary: me, name, family, friend, happy, sad
tuesday.circleTime: Read a page from I Like Myself! Affirm: every circle is enough.
tuesday.outdoorPlay: Chalk personal circles; place leaf tokens for caring people.
tuesday.familyConnection: Send belonging-circle photo (with permission) and portrait progress.
tuesday.observations: Notes belonging language; notes portrait color choices.
tuesday.adaptations: Picture cards for circles; seated movement options.

items.title: People in My Circle
items.objective: Show people, pets, and helpers who care for me. Keep every circle equally special.
items.description: Each child fills a personal circle with stickers or dots for trusted people. Circles stay personal and equally special.
items.materials:
Paper with a large open circle per child
Stickers or paper dots
Picture cards of caring roles (teacher, sibling, neighbor, pet)
items.setup: One circle per child. Use personal circles instead of shared ranked columns. Model placing two dots for people who care for you.
items.steps:
1. Child names someone who cares for them.
2. Places a dot inside their own circle.
3. May add pets, teachers, or neighbors.
4. Optional: dictate ‘In my circle I have…’
5. Display circles side by side as equally special.
items.teacherRole: Coach belonging language. Pause ‘who has more’ talk. Celebrate each circle as enough.
items.teacherLanguage: Who helps you feel safe? Anyone else belongs in your circle? Every circle is special.
items.observationOpportunities:
Names caring people or pets
Includes teachers or neighbors
Responds kindly when a peer’s circle looks different
items.extensions: Dictate one sentence: ‘In my circle I have…’
items.adaptations: Offer picture cards of caring roles to point to.
items.supportAdaptations: Teacher scribes names while child places dots.
items.additionalChallenge: Child tells one way someone in their circle helps them.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers place dots with help; preschoolers dictate sentences.
items.differentiation: Support: picture cards. Challenge: dictate a belonging sentence.
items.cleanupTip: Clip circles to the gallery string for family pickup.

items.title: Body Part Movement Game
items.objective: Move body parts in inclusive ways—including seated and wheeled options.
items.description: Follow-the-leader movement with adapted choices for every body.
items.materials:
Open space
Picture cues for move / stop
Optional rhythm instrument
items.setup: Post adaptive options (wave elbows, roll wheels, tip toes). Model without spotlighting.
items.steps:
1. Call a body part with an inclusive option.
2. Children move in their own way.
3. Freeze on cue.
4. Children suggest the next move.
items.teacherRole: Offer alternatives aloud so every body is included.
items.teacherLanguage: Can you wiggle fingers—or tap the tray? Wheels can roll forward and stop.
items.observationOpportunities:
Chooses an adaptation without shame
Suggests moves for friends
items.extensions: Children invent a two-move pattern.
items.adaptations: Seated or wheeled versions for every call.
items.additionalChallenge: Lead a round for the group.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers copy one move; preschoolers invent.
items.cleanupTip: Stack cue cards in the movement bin.

items.title: Self-Portrait Studio
items.objective: Create a process self-portrait with skin-tone crayons—no adult model to copy.
items.description: Mirrors nearby; scribbles and unique features celebrated.
items.materials:
Paper
Skin-tone crayons and markers
Mirrors
Optional yarn for hair textures
items.setup: No adult sample portrait. Set mirrors and inclusive crayons.
items.steps:
1. Look in the mirror.
2. Draw freely.
3. Add hair, aids, or favorite shirt details.
4. Dictate a name for the portrait.
items.teacherRole: Refuse ‘fix it’ corrections; narrate what the child chose.
items.teacherLanguage: What color feels like you today? Tell me about your hair.
items.observationOpportunities:
Includes vision aids or wheels if used
Comfort looking in mirror while drawing
items.extensions: Add a dictated ‘I like…’ sentence.
items.adaptations: Stamp circle face; child adds features.
items.supportAdaptations: Teacher outlines oval if requested; child fills.
items.additionalChallenge: Draw a friend with permission.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers scribble; preschoolers add details.
items.cleanupTip: Portrait drying rack.

tuesday.teacherPreparation: Prepare one circle per child—no ranked columns. Post adaptive movement options.
tuesday.activityFlow: People in My Circle → Body Part Movement Game → Self-Portrait Studio.
tuesday.questions: Who helps you feel safe? How can wheels or feet join this move?
tuesday.observationFocus: Belonging language; interruption of ‘who has more’; inclusive movement.

wednesday.theme: Caring Play, Kind Questions, Name Letters
wednesday.objectives:
Invent open family/care roles.
Interview a friend kindly.
Hunt letters from my name.
wednesday.materials:
Dramatic play kitchen props
Interview prompt cards
Letter cards and decoys
wednesday.vocabulary: me, name, family, friend, happy, sad
wednesday.circleTime: Model one interview question. Practice listening bodies.
wednesday.outdoorPlay: Outdoor dramatic-play picnic roles; letter hunt on a fence line.
wednesday.familyConnection: Share one kind question children asked a friend.
wednesday.safetyNotes: Large letter cards; choke-safe play food.

items.title: Family Dramatic Play
items.objective: Act out caring roles children invent—without assigned ‘mom/dad only’ scripts.
items.description: Open role naming: cook, helper, baby, neighbor, pet caregiver, etc.
items.materials:
Play kitchen
Dolls
Phones
Soft props
Picture cards of roles
items.setup: Remove props that force one family mold. Post open role cards.
items.steps:
1. Children choose roles.
2. Play a care routine (meal, bedtime, hello).
3. Switch roles.
4. Clean the play home together.
items.teacherRole: Coach consent and flexible roles; interrupt stereotypes gently.
items.teacherLanguage: Who are you in the story today? How do you help your people?
items.observationOpportunities:
Role flexibility
Care themes vs power themes
items.extensions: Invite a stuffed pet to the family.
items.adaptations: Picture role cards for nonverbal choosers.
items.additionalChallenge: Children write a menu or shopping list.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers cook beside; preschoolers assign jobs.
items.cleanupTip: Reset kitchen with a closing song.

items.title: Friend Interview
items.objective: Ask a friend one kind question and listen to the answer.
items.description: Safe picture prompts only—no private family quizzes.
items.materials:
Interview clipboards
Picture prompt cards (favorite color, pet, food, game)
Pencils
items.setup: Model one question. Pair children. Keep prompts about preferences.
items.steps:
1. Choose a prompt card.
2. Ask the friend.
3. Listen and mark or draw the answer.
4. Switch roles.
items.teacherRole: Coach listening bodies; redirect invasive questions.
items.teacherLanguage: What is your favorite…? I heard you—thank you for telling me.
items.observationOpportunities:
Waits for answer
Remembers peer’s favorite later
items.extensions: Share one learned favorite at circle.
items.adaptations: Point to cards instead of speaking.
items.additionalChallenge: Invent a new kind question.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers answer with pointing; preschoolers scribe.
items.cleanupTip: Clipboards back to the literacy shelf.

items.title: Name Letter Hunt
items.objective: Hunt letters from my name among decoy letters.
items.description: Room hunt for name letters—no races.
items.materials:
Letter cards from each child’s name
Decoy letters
Baskets
items.setup: Hide 3–5 letters per child plus decoys. No timers.
items.steps:
1. Review own letters.
2. Hunt and collect.
3. Check against name card.
4. Celebrate finds—not speed.
items.teacherRole: Block racing language; help verify matches.
items.teacherLanguage: Does this letter live in your name? Check your card.
items.observationOpportunities:
Uses name card as reference
Shares finds with peers
items.extensions: Build the name on the floor with finds.
items.adaptations: Color-code the child’s letters.
items.additionalChallenge: Find a friend’s first letter too.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers hunt photo cards; preschoolers hunt letters.
items.cleanupTip: Sort letters into name envelopes.

wednesday.teacherPreparation: Remove forced mom/dad-only props. Hide name letters (no timers).
wednesday.activityFlow: Family Dramatic Play → Friend Interview → Name Letter Hunt.
wednesday.questions: Who are you in the story today? What is your friend’s favorite…?
wednesday.observationFocus: Role flexibility; listening; letter matching without racing.

thursday.theme: Towers We Measure, Feelings We Show, Books We Make
thursday.objectives:
Measure block towers rather than children’s heights.
Express feelings through art.
Make a three-page All About Me book.
thursday.materials:
Blocks
Cubes/yarn
Feeling cards
Folded books
Crayons
Adult stapler (away from children)
thursday.vocabulary: me, name, family, friend, happy, sad
thursday.circleTime: Wiggle What You Will with adaptive options. Preview tower measuring.
thursday.outdoorPlay: Build stick towers and measure with yarn outdoors.
thursday.familyConnection: Send book home or photo of tower label ‘my tower.’
thursday.adaptations: Tray building; stamp faces; one-page books.
thursday.safetyNotes: Tip-safe tower zones; adult stapler away from children.

items.title: Build & Measure My Tower
items.objective: Build a block tower and measure it with cubes or yarn. Measure structures only.
items.description: Children build ‘my tower,’ measure with non-standard units, and label the tower. Skip lining children up by height.
items.materials:
Blocks
Linking cubes or yarn
Sticky notes
Floor space
items.setup: Clear floor. Cubes in a bowl. Keep wall charts that rank children’s height out of this center.
items.steps:
1. Build a tower.
2. Measure with cubes or yarn beside the tower.
3. Count units with support.
4. Label sticky note ‘my tower.’
5. Optional: rebuild taller or wider—still measuring the structure.
items.teacherRole: Keep talk on towers. Redirect child-to-child height talk back to the blocks.
items.teacherLanguage: How many cubes tall is your tower? What happens if we add one block?
items.observationOpportunities:
Measures tower not body
Counts cubes with pointing
Stays focused on structure talk
items.extensions: Check two towers’ cube counts—structures only.
items.adaptations: Build on a tray for stability.
items.supportAdaptations: Teacher counts aloud while child points.
items.additionalChallenge: Record cube count on the sticky note.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers stack; preschoolers measure and label.
items.cleanupTip: Blocks sorted by shape; cubes in the bowl.

items.title: Feelings Faces Art
items.objective: Show a feeling with process art—mixed feelings allowed.
items.description: Optional emotion cues; children may show more than one feeling.
items.materials:
Paper
Crayons
Optional feeling cards
Mirrors
items.setup: Feeling cards available, not required. No ‘correct’ face.
items.steps:
1. Name a feeling or pick a card.
2. Draw or collage the feeling.
3. Optional: add a second feeling.
4. Dictate a label.
items.teacherRole: Validate all feelings; avoid fixing ‘sad’ art.
items.teacherLanguage: What feeling is visiting you? It’s okay to have two.
items.observationOpportunities:
Uses feeling words
Chooses mixed feelings
Comfort sharing or keeping private
items.extensions: Add a calm-down strategy drawing on the back.
items.adaptations: Point to a card; teacher draws with child.
items.additionalChallenge: Explain what helps when that feeling comes.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers scribble feelings; preschoolers label.
items.cleanupTip: Feeling cards into a calm corner basket.

items.title: All About Me Book Making
items.objective: Make a three-page book about me—scribbles count as writing.
items.description: Pages: my name, people I love, something I like. Dictation welcome.
items.materials:
Folded paper books
Crayons
Stickers
Adult stapler (away from children)
items.setup: Pre-fold books. Model scribble writing as valid.
items.steps:
1. Page 1: name/portrait.
2. Page 2: people or pets.
3. Page 3: favorite thing.
4. Dictate captions; staple with adult tool away from kids.
items.teacherRole: Scribe on request; celebrate scribbles.
items.teacherLanguage: What should this page say? Your marks tell your story.
items.observationOpportunities:
Chooses people freely
Scribble vs letter-like marks
Pride in book
items.extensions: Read the book to a friend.
items.adaptations: Photo glued on page 1 if drawing is hard today.
items.safetyNotes: Adult uses stapler away from children.
items.additionalChallenge: Add a fourth page: ‘I can help by…’
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers one page; preschoolers three.
items.cleanupTip: Books into take-home mailbox.

thursday.teacherPreparation: Remove comparative height displays from this center. Prefold books.
thursday.activityFlow: Build & Measure My Tower → Feelings Faces Art → All About Me Book Making.
thursday.questions: How many cubes tall is your tower? What feeling is visiting you?
thursday.observationFocus: Tower-not-body measuring; mixed feelings allowed; scribble writing honored.

friday.objectives:
Travel a cooperative scarf path.
Celebrate with opt-in sharing.
Parade with inclusive leaders.
friday.materials:
Scarves
Painter’s tape
Name cards
Portraits
Optional instruments
friday.vocabulary: me, name, family, friend, happy, sad
friday.outdoorPlay: Chalk scarf path on pavement; parade to the garden and back.
friday.familyConnection: Send affirmation lyrics and portrait photo per permission.
friday.safetyNotes: Wide lanes; walking feet; clear thresholds.

items.title: Friendship Scarf Path
items.objective: Design and travel a cooperative scarf pathway wide enough for every friend.
items.description: Children help tape a wide path, choose moves, and take turns leading—including mobility-device users as leaders.
items.materials:
Scarves or streamers
Painter’s tape or chalk
Open path wide enough for mobility devices
items.setup: Children help lay a wide path. Mark start/finish. Practice one gentle move.
items.steps:
1. Build the path together.
2. Choose a move (walk, roll, side-step, dance).
3. Travel the path.
4. New leader chooses the next move.
5. End with a group scarf wave.
items.teacherRole: Keep path wide; invite wheelchair/walker leaders; skip outline tracing games.
items.teacherLanguage: Who wants to lead the next move? Make space for every friend.
items.observationOpportunities:
Includes friends using mobility devices
Negotiates turns leading
Keeps path clear
items.extensions: Add a scarf color pattern along the path.
items.adaptations: Shorter path; seated scarf waves at stations.
items.safetyNotes: Wide lanes; no racing; clear thresholds.
items.additionalChallenge: Children map the path on paper after.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers walk a short tape line; preschoolers design.
items.cleanupTip: Roll tape; scarves to laundry basket.

items.title: Celebration Circle
items.objective: Celebrate belonging with opt-in sharing and kind listening.
items.description: Children may share one pride moment or hold a name card quietly while peers cheer.
items.materials:
Name cards
Optional celebration stickers
Soft drum or clap pattern
items.setup: Explain opt-in. Practice clap pattern for listeners.
items.steps:
1. Affirmation chant.
2. Opt-in shares.
3. Classmates clap or sign applause.
4. Close with belonging words.
items.teacherRole: Protect opt-out; coach kind listening.
items.teacherLanguage: You may share or hold your card. We celebrate every friend.
items.observationOpportunities:
Chooses share or quiet hold
Peer kindness
Affirmation language spreading
items.extensions: Sing I Am Me affirmation again.
items.adaptations: Point to a picture card instead of speaking.
items.supportAdaptations: Whisper share to teacher who announces.
items.additionalChallenge: Child offers a compliment to a peer.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers wave name cards; preschoolers share words.
items.cleanupTip: Name cards to take-home.

items.title: All About Me Movement Parade
items.objective: Parade with portraits or name cards—mobility-device leaders included.
items.description: Walking parade with a rolling path segment led by wheelchair users when present.
items.materials:
Portraits or name cards
Scarves
Optional rhythm instruments
Clear thresholds
items.setup: Map a walking/rolling loop. Offer instruments or clapping.
items.steps:
1. Line up with space for devices.
2. Leader segment rotates.
3. Parade once.
4. Wave to classroom ‘audience.’
items.teacherRole: Rotate leaders; keep walking feet; clear thresholds.
items.teacherLanguage: Leaders show the pace. Make room—wheels and feet together.
items.observationOpportunities:
How leaders include friends behind
Tempo that keeps group regulated
items.extensions: Wave to plants or pets as audience.
items.adaptations: Flag wave from a chair.
items.additionalChallenge: Child invents a clap pattern for the parade.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers parade a short hallway; preschoolers plan route.
items.cleanupTip: Instruments to shadow board.

friday.teacherPreparation: Map a wide rolling/walking path. Practice opt-in celebration language.
friday.activityFlow: Friendship Scarf Path → Celebration Circle → All About Me Movement Parade.
friday.questions: Who will lead the next path move? What are you proud of this week?
friday.observationFocus: Inclusive leading; opt-in comfort; parade regulation.

tuesday.observations: Notes belonging language; notes portrait color choices.
tuesday.adaptations: Picture cards for circles; seated movement options.

items.title: People in My Circle
items.objective: Show people, pets, and helpers who care for me. Keep every circle equally special.
items.description: Each child fills a personal circle with stickers or dots for trusted people. Circles stay personal and equally special.
items.materials:
Paper with a large open circle per child
Stickers or paper dots
Picture cards of caring roles (teacher, sibling, neighbor, pet)
items.setup: One circle per child. Use personal circles instead of shared ranked columns. Model placing two dots for people who care for you.
items.steps:
1. Child names someone who cares for them.
2. Places a dot inside their own circle.
3. May add pets, teachers, or neighbors.
4. Optional: dictate ‘In my circle I have…’
5. Display circles side by side as equally special.
items.teacherRole: Coach belonging language. Pause ‘who has more’ talk. Celebrate each circle as enough.
items.teacherLanguage: Who helps you feel safe? Anyone else belongs in your circle? Every circle is special.
items.observationOpportunities:
Names caring people or pets
Includes teachers or neighbors
Responds kindly when a peer’s circle looks different
items.extensions: Dictate one sentence: ‘In my circle I have…’
items.adaptations: Offer picture cards of caring roles to point to.
items.supportAdaptations: Teacher scribes names while child places dots.
items.additionalChallenge: Child tells one way someone in their circle helps them.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers place dots with help; preschoolers dictate sentences.
items.differentiation: Support: picture cards. Challenge: dictate a belonging sentence.
items.cleanupTip: Clip circles to the gallery string for family pickup.

items.title: Body Part Movement Game
items.objective: Move body parts in inclusive ways—including seated and wheeled options.
items.description: Follow-the-leader movement with adapted choices for every body.
items.materials:
Open space
Picture cues for move / stop
Optional rhythm instrument
items.setup: Post adaptive options (wave elbows, roll wheels, tip toes). Model without spotlighting.
items.steps:
1. Call a body part with an inclusive option.
2. Children move in their own way.
3. Freeze on cue.
4. Children suggest the next move.
items.teacherRole: Offer alternatives aloud so every body is included.
items.teacherLanguage: Can you wiggle fingers—or tap the tray? Wheels can roll forward and stop.
items.observationOpportunities:
Chooses an adaptation without shame
Suggests moves for friends
items.extensions: Children invent a two-move pattern.
items.adaptations: Seated or wheeled versions for every call.
items.additionalChallenge: Lead a round for the group.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers copy one move; preschoolers invent.
items.cleanupTip: Stack cue cards in the movement bin.

items.title: Self-Portrait Studio
items.objective: Create a process self-portrait with skin-tone crayons—no adult model to copy.
items.description: Mirrors nearby; scribbles and unique features celebrated.
items.materials:
Paper
Skin-tone crayons and markers
Mirrors
Optional yarn for hair textures
items.setup: No adult sample portrait. Set mirrors and inclusive crayons.
items.steps:
1. Look in the mirror.
2. Draw freely.
3. Add hair, aids, or favorite shirt details.
4. Dictate a name for the portrait.
items.teacherRole: Refuse ‘fix it’ corrections; narrate what the child chose.
items.teacherLanguage: What color feels like you today? Tell me about your hair.
items.observationOpportunities:
Includes vision aids or wheels if used
Comfort looking in mirror while drawing
items.extensions: Add a dictated ‘I like…’ sentence.
items.adaptations: Stamp circle face; child adds features.
items.supportAdaptations: Teacher outlines oval if requested; child fills.
items.additionalChallenge: Draw a friend with permission.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers scribble; preschoolers add details.
items.cleanupTip: Portrait drying rack.

tuesday.teacherPreparation: Prepare one circle per child—no ranked columns. Post adaptive movement options.
tuesday.activityFlow: People in My Circle → Body Part Movement Game → Self-Portrait Studio.
tuesday.questions: Who helps you feel safe? How can wheels or feet join this move?
tuesday.observationFocus: Belonging language; interruption of ‘who has more’; inclusive movement.

wednesday.theme: Caring Play, Kind Questions, Name Letters
wednesday.objectives:
Invent open family/care roles.
Interview a friend kindly.
Hunt letters from my name.
wednesday.materials:
Dramatic play kitchen props
Interview prompt cards
Letter cards and decoys
wednesday.vocabulary: me, name, family, friend, happy, sad
wednesday.circleTime: Model one interview question. Practice listening bodies.
wednesday.outdoorPlay: Outdoor dramatic-play picnic roles; letter hunt on a fence line.
wednesday.familyConnection: Share one kind question children asked a friend.
wednesday.safetyNotes: Large letter cards; choke-safe play food.

items.title: Family Dramatic Play
items.objective: Act out caring roles children invent—without assigned ‘mom/dad only’ scripts.
items.description: Open role naming: cook, helper, baby, neighbor, pet caregiver, etc.
items.materials:
Play kitchen
Dolls
Phones
Soft props
Picture cards of roles
items.setup: Remove props that force one family mold. Post open role cards.
items.steps:
1. Children choose roles.
2. Play a care routine (meal, bedtime, hello).
3. Switch roles.
4. Clean the play home together.
items.teacherRole: Coach consent and flexible roles; interrupt stereotypes gently.
items.teacherLanguage: Who are you in the story today? How do you help your people?
items.observationOpportunities:
Role flexibility
Care themes vs power themes
items.extensions: Invite a stuffed pet to the family.
items.adaptations: Picture role cards for nonverbal choosers.
items.additionalChallenge: Children write a menu or shopping list.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers cook beside; preschoolers assign jobs.
items.cleanupTip: Reset kitchen with a closing song.

items.title: Friend Interview
items.objective: Ask a friend one kind question and listen to the answer.
items.description: Safe picture prompts only—no private family quizzes.
items.materials:
Interview clipboards
Picture prompt cards (favorite color, pet, food, game)
Pencils
items.setup: Model one question. Pair children. Keep prompts about preferences.
items.steps:
1. Choose a prompt card.
2. Ask the friend.
3. Listen and mark or draw the answer.
4. Switch roles.
items.teacherRole: Coach listening bodies; redirect invasive questions.
items.teacherLanguage: What is your favorite…? I heard you—thank you for telling me.
items.observationOpportunities:
Waits for answer
Remembers peer’s favorite later
items.extensions: Share one learned favorite at circle.
items.adaptations: Point to cards instead of speaking.
items.additionalChallenge: Invent a new kind question.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers answer with pointing; preschoolers scribe.
items.cleanupTip: Clipboards back to the literacy shelf.

items.title: Name Letter Hunt
items.objective: Hunt letters from my name among decoy letters.
items.description: Room hunt for name letters—no races.
items.materials:
Letter cards from each child’s name
Decoy letters
Baskets
items.setup: Hide 3–5 letters per child plus decoys. No timers.
items.steps:
1. Review own letters.
2. Hunt and collect.
3. Check against name card.
4. Celebrate finds—not speed.
items.teacherRole: Block racing language; help verify matches.
items.teacherLanguage: Does this letter live in your name? Check your card.
items.observationOpportunities:
Uses name card as reference
Shares finds with peers
items.extensions: Build the name on the floor with finds.
items.adaptations: Color-code the child’s letters.
items.additionalChallenge: Find a friend’s first letter too.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers hunt photo cards; preschoolers hunt letters.
items.cleanupTip: Sort letters into name envelopes.

wednesday.teacherPreparation: Remove forced mom/dad-only props. Hide name letters (no timers).
wednesday.activityFlow: Family Dramatic Play → Friend Interview → Name Letter Hunt.
wednesday.questions: Who are you in the story today? What is your friend’s favorite…?
wednesday.observationFocus: Role flexibility; listening; letter matching without racing.

thursday.theme: Towers We Measure, Feelings We Show, Books We Make
thursday.objectives:
Measure block towers rather than children’s heights.
Express feelings through art.
Make a three-page All About Me book.
thursday.materials:
Blocks
Cubes/yarn
Feeling cards
Folded books
Crayons
Adult stapler (away from children)
thursday.vocabulary: me, name, family, friend, happy, sad
thursday.circleTime: Wiggle What You Will with adaptive options. Preview tower measuring.
thursday.outdoorPlay: Build stick towers and measure with yarn outdoors.
thursday.familyConnection: Send book home or photo of tower label ‘my tower.’
thursday.adaptations: Tray building; stamp faces; one-page books.
thursday.safetyNotes: Tip-safe tower zones; adult stapler away from children.

items.title: Build & Measure My Tower
items.objective: Build a block tower and measure it with cubes or yarn. Measure structures only.
items.description: Children build ‘my tower,’ measure with non-standard units, and label the tower. Skip lining children up by height.
items.materials:
Blocks
Linking cubes or yarn
Sticky notes
Floor space
items.setup: Clear floor. Cubes in a bowl. Keep wall charts that rank children’s height out of this center.
items.steps:
1. Build a tower.
2. Measure with cubes or yarn beside the tower.
3. Count units with support.
4. Label sticky note ‘my tower.’
5. Optional: rebuild taller or wider—still measuring the structure.
items.teacherRole: Keep talk on towers. Redirect child-to-child height talk back to the blocks.
items.teacherLanguage: How many cubes tall is your tower? What happens if we add one block?
items.observationOpportunities:
Measures tower not body
Counts cubes with pointing
Stays focused on structure talk
items.extensions: Check two towers’ cube counts—structures only.
items.adaptations: Build on a tray for stability.
items.supportAdaptations: Teacher counts aloud while child points.
items.additionalChallenge: Record cube count on the sticky note.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers stack; preschoolers measure and label.
items.cleanupTip: Blocks sorted by shape; cubes in the bowl.

items.title: Feelings Faces Art
items.objective: Show a feeling with process art—mixed feelings allowed.
items.description: Optional emotion cues; children may show more than one feeling.
items.materials:
Paper
Crayons
Optional feeling cards
Mirrors
items.setup: Feeling cards available, not required. No ‘correct’ face.
items.steps:
1. Name a feeling or pick a card.
2. Draw or collage the feeling.
3. Optional: add a second feeling.
4. Dictate a label.
items.teacherRole: Validate all feelings; avoid fixing ‘sad’ art.
items.teacherLanguage: What feeling is visiting you? It’s okay to have two.
items.observationOpportunities:
Uses feeling words
Chooses mixed feelings
Comfort sharing or keeping private
items.extensions: Add a calm-down strategy drawing on the back.
items.adaptations: Point to a card; teacher draws with child.
items.additionalChallenge: Explain what helps when that feeling comes.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers scribble feelings; preschoolers label.
items.cleanupTip: Feeling cards into a calm corner basket.

items.title: All About Me Book Making
items.objective: Make a three-page book about me—scribbles count as writing.
items.description: Pages: my name, people I love, something I like. Dictation welcome.
items.materials:
Folded paper books
Crayons
Stickers
Adult stapler (away from children)
items.setup: Pre-fold books. Model scribble writing as valid.
items.steps:
1. Page 1: name/portrait.
2. Page 2: people or pets.
3. Page 3: favorite thing.
4. Dictate captions; staple with adult tool away from kids.
items.teacherRole: Scribe on request; celebrate scribbles.
items.teacherLanguage: What should this page say? Your marks tell your story.
items.observationOpportunities:
Chooses people freely
Scribble vs letter-like marks
Pride in book
items.extensions: Read the book to a friend.
items.adaptations: Photo glued on page 1 if drawing is hard today.
items.safetyNotes: Adult uses stapler away from children.
items.additionalChallenge: Add a fourth page: ‘I can help by…’
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers one page; preschoolers three.
items.cleanupTip: Books into take-home mailbox.

thursday.teacherPreparation: Remove comparative height displays from this center. Prefold books.
thursday.activityFlow: Build & Measure My Tower → Feelings Faces Art → All About Me Book Making.
thursday.questions: How many cubes tall is your tower? What feeling is visiting you?
thursday.observationFocus: Tower-not-body measuring; mixed feelings allowed; scribble writing honored.

friday.objectives:
Travel a cooperative scarf path.
Celebrate with opt-in sharing.
Parade with inclusive leaders.
friday.materials:
Scarves
Painter’s tape
Name cards
Portraits
Optional instruments
friday.vocabulary: me, name, family, friend, happy, sad
friday.outdoorPlay: Chalk scarf path on pavement; parade to the garden and back.
friday.familyConnection: Send affirmation lyrics and portrait photo per permission.
friday.safetyNotes: Wide lanes; walking feet; clear thresholds.

items.title: Friendship Scarf Path
items.objective: Design and travel a cooperative scarf pathway wide enough for every friend.
items.description: Children help tape a wide path, choose moves, and take turns leading—including mobility-device users as leaders.
items.materials:
Scarves or streamers
Painter’s tape or chalk
Open path wide enough for mobility devices
items.setup: Children help lay a wide path. Mark start/finish. Practice one gentle move.
items.steps:
1. Build the path together.
2. Choose a move (walk, roll, side-step, dance).
3. Travel the path.
4. New leader chooses the next move.
5. End with a group scarf wave.
items.teacherRole: Keep path wide; invite wheelchair/walker leaders; skip outline tracing games.
items.teacherLanguage: Who wants to lead the next move? Make space for every friend.
items.observationOpportunities:
Includes friends using mobility devices
Negotiates turns leading
Keeps path clear
items.extensions: Add a scarf color pattern along the path.
items.adaptations: Shorter path; seated scarf waves at stations.
items.safetyNotes: Wide lanes; no racing; clear thresholds.
items.additionalChallenge: Children map the path on paper after.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers walk a short tape line; preschoolers design.
items.cleanupTip: Roll tape; scarves to laundry basket.

items.title: Celebration Circle
items.objective: Celebrate belonging with opt-in sharing and kind listening.
items.description: Children may share one pride moment or hold a name card quietly while peers cheer.
items.materials:
Name cards
Optional celebration stickers
Soft drum or clap pattern
items.setup: Explain opt-in. Practice clap pattern for listeners.
items.steps:
1. Affirmation chant.
2. Opt-in shares.
3. Classmates clap or sign applause.
4. Close with belonging words.
items.teacherRole: Protect opt-out; coach kind listening.
items.teacherLanguage: You may share or hold your card. We celebrate every friend.
items.observationOpportunities:
Chooses share or quiet hold
Peer kindness
Affirmation language spreading
items.extensions: Sing I Am Me affirmation again.
items.adaptations: Point to a picture card instead of speaking.
items.supportAdaptations: Whisper share to teacher who announces.
items.additionalChallenge: Child offers a compliment to a peer.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers wave name cards; preschoolers share words.
items.cleanupTip: Name cards to take-home.

items.title: All About Me Movement Parade
items.objective: Parade with portraits or name cards—mobility-device leaders included.
items.description: Walking parade with a rolling path segment led by wheelchair users when present.
items.materials:
Portraits or name cards
Scarves
Optional rhythm instruments
Clear thresholds
items.setup: Map a walking/rolling loop. Offer instruments or clapping.
items.steps:
1. Line up with space for devices.
2. Leader segment rotates.
3. Parade once.
4. Wave to classroom ‘audience.’
items.teacherRole: Rotate leaders; keep walking feet; clear thresholds.
items.teacherLanguage: Leaders show the pace. Make room—wheels and feet together.
items.observationOpportunities:
How leaders include friends behind
Tempo that keeps group regulated
items.extensions: Wave to plants or pets as audience.
items.adaptations: Flag wave from a chair.
items.additionalChallenge: Child invents a clap pattern for the parade.
items.mixedAgeAdaptations: Toddlers parade a short hallway; preschoolers plan route.
items.cleanupTip: Instruments to shadow board.

friday.teacherPreparation: Map a wide rolling/walking path. Practice opt-in celebration language.
friday.activityFlow: Friendship Scarf Path → Celebration Circle → All About Me Movement Parade.
friday.questions: Who will lead the next path move? What are you proud of this week?
friday.observationFocus: Inclusive leading; opt-in comfort; parade regulation.

cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.imageRequirementReason: Mirror play is familiar; no photo needed.
teacherTips: Sit beside the child at mirror height; copy their expression before asking them to copy yours.
Keep emotion cards face-down until the child is engaged with their own reflection.

substitutions.use: stainless cookie sheets or acrylic mirror tiles with taped edges
All About Me Picture Card Pack face cards

observationPrompts: Does the child notice the teacher’s matching face?
Which expression do they sustain longest?
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.indoorAlternatives: Use a wall mirror with floor cushions.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.outdoorAlternatives: Notice reflections in a window on a cloudy day.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.adaptations: For mirror-averse children, play peek-a-boo with a scarf first.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.extensions: Take turns being the leader of faces.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.cleanupTip: Wipe mirrors with child-safe cleaner after the group.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.safetyNotes: Use acrylic or metal mirrors only. Tape edges. Supervise to avoid hitting mirrors.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.setup: Stage materials for “Mirror Me” at one low table or rug spot before inviting children.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.steps: Invite children into “Mirror Me”. Model once, then narrate child moves. Close with the activity’s own cleanup tip.

sentence strips with a small symbol sticker unique to each child

Do they seek the first letter by shape or by asking?
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.indoorAlternatives: Tape name cards to blocks for a find-and-stack game.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.outdoorAlternatives: Write names in sand or chalk; children place a leaf on their name.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.adaptations: Partner with a friend to hunt letters in a mutual search.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.extensions: Trace the first letter on each other’s palm with permission.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.cleanupTip: Store each child’s card in a labeled envelope for Friday parade.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.safetyNotes: Magnets large enough to fail choke test. No small fridge magnets.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.setup: Stage materials for “My Name Discovery” at one low table or rug spot before inviting children.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.steps: Invite children into “My Name Discovery”. Model once, then narrate child moves. Close with the activity’s own cleanup tip.

cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.imageRequirementReason: Conversation about family photos is relationship-based, not setup-dependent.
teacherTips: Accept drawings or magazine cutouts if a photo is unavailable—every family is representable.
Never require children to explain family structures; let them point and name freely.

substitutions.use: All About Me family picture cards plus child-made drawings
a string with clothespins at child height

observationPrompts: Whom does the child choose to name first?
Do they show interest in a peer’s photo?
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.indoorAlternatives: Share in pairs on the rug.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.outdoorAlternatives: Clip photos to a fence line for a walking gallery.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.adaptations: Teacher holds the photo while the child points.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.extensions: Add a sticky note with one word the child dictates.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.cleanupTip: Return photos to labeled envelopes immediately.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.safetyNotes: Respect privacy—no posting photos publicly without permission.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.setup: Stage materials for “Family Photo Sharing” at one low table or rug spot before inviting children.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:monday:ite.steps: Invite children into “Family Photo Sharing”. Model once, then narrate child moves. Close with the activity’s own cleanup tip.

cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:tuesday:it.imageRequirementReason: Sticker chart about people we love is verbal/social; no image required.
teacherTips: Columns are ‘people who care for me’ categories children invent—not ranked family sizes.
Skip comparing who has ‘more’ people; celebrate each circle as enough.

substitutions.use: a cardboard trifold with three open circles drawn

observationPrompts: Does the child include teachers or pets in their circle?
How do they react if a peer’s circle looks different?
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:tuesday:it.indoorAlternatives: Build circles with yarn loops on the floor and place name cards inside.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:tuesday:it.outdoorAlternatives: Chalk circles on pavement for each child to stand in with a friend.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:tuesday:it.adaptations: Offer picture cards of caring roles (teacher, sibling, neighbor).
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:tuesday:it.extensions: Dictate one sentence: ‘In my circle I have…’
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:tuesday:it.cleanupTip: Photograph the chart for portfolios; avoid public hallway posting without consent.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:tuesday:it.safetyNotes: No forced disclosure of household details.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:tuesday:it.setup: Stage materials for “People in My Circle” at one low table or rug spot before inviting children.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:tuesday:it.steps: Invite children into “People in My Circle”. Model once, then narrate child moves. Close with the activity’s own cleanup tip.

teacherTips: Use inclusive language: ‘move the part that helps you wave’ if a child has limb differences.
Follow Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes slowly; invite seated marching alternatives.

substitutions.use: All About Me emotion/interest cards as movement cues instead
stand-behind-chair movements in a tight room

observationPrompts: Does the child watch peers or the teacher for cues?
Which movements do they invent beyond the song?
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:tuesday:it.outdoorAlternatives: Move across playground zones per body-part cue.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:tuesday:it.adaptations: Offer only two cues for children who need fewer switches.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:tuesday:it.extensions: Children take turns being the caller.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:tuesday:it.cleanupTip: Collect cards into a binder sleeve.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:tuesday:it.safetyNotes: No forcing range of motion. Honor adaptive equipment pathways.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:tuesday:it.setup: Stage materials for “Body Part Movement Game” at one low table or rug spot before inviting children.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:tuesday:it.steps: Invite children into “Body Part Movement Game”. Model once, then narrate child moves. Close with the activity’s own cleanup tip.

cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:tuesday:it.adaptations: Dictate labels for marks if drawing is frustrating.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:tuesday:it.extensions: Add a speech bubble with a favorite word.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:tuesday:it.cleanupTip: Dry racks labeled with name cards from Monday.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:tuesday:it.safetyNotes: Non-toxic colors. No glitter near eyes.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:tuesday:it.setup: Stage materials for “Self-Portrait Studio” at one low table or rug spot before inviting children.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:tuesday:it.steps: Invite children into “Self-Portrait Studio”. Model once, then narrate child moves. Close with the activity’s own cleanup tip.

cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:wednesday:.imageRequirementReason: Home living props are familiar; optional photo only for unique prop layouts.
teacherTips: Stock diverse family figure sets and the Picture Card Pack family cards in the kitchen.

substitutions.use: laundry basket stove and cardboard box fridge

observationPrompts: How do children negotiate caregiving roles?
What caregiving language appears?
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:wednesday:.indoorAlternatives: Bring a baby-doll bath basin to the table.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:wednesday:.adaptations: Visual schedule cards for play routines (cook → eat → rest).
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:wednesday:.extensions: Call the block area on a toy phone to invite neighbors.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:wednesday:.cleanupTip: Sort dishes and dolls into separate caddies.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:wednesday:.safetyNotes: No real hot liquids. Doll accessories choke-tested.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:wednesday:.setup: Stage materials for “Family Dramatic Play” at one low table or rug spot before inviting children.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:wednesday:.steps: Invite children into “Family Dramatic Play”. Model once, then narrate child moves. Close with the activity’s own cleanup tip.

teacherTips: Picture prompts only—favorite color, play, food—never intrusive home questions.
Pairs sit knee-to-knee; teacher scribes if needed.

substitutions.use: All About Me interest cards as question prompts

observationPrompts: Does the child wait for an answer before next question?
How do they show listening (nod, repeat, point)?
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:wednesday:.indoorAlternatives: Interview stuffed animals first as practice.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:wednesday:.outdoorAlternatives: Interview on a walking path with stop spots.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:wednesday:.adaptations: Yes/no picture choices for emergent speakers.
cur-lp-preschool-all-about-me:wednesday:.extensions: Share one learned favorite at closing circle.

week.weeklyOverview: Preschoolers study identity through mirrors, names, chosen families, feelings art, and cooperative movement. We avoid body comparisons and celebrate many ways to look, move, and belong.
week.weeklyMaterials:
Child-safe mirrors
Name cards and chunky letters
Family photos or drawings
Skin-tone crayons
Paper and clipboards
Blocks and cubes
Scarves and ribbon
Picture card pack PDF
Stickers or paper dots
Stapler (adult)
Play kitchen props
Emotion/interest cards
week.teacherPreparation: Print All About Me Picture Card Pack. Request optional family photos with privacy note. Set skin-tone crayons out. Replace any height charts that rank children.
week.familyConnection: Invite families to send a drawing or photo of people/pets who care for the child, or to share a preferred name pronunciation audio.
milestones: Language: Uses name and feeling words
SEL: Shows interest in peers’ preferences
Cognition: Matches letters in own name
Motor: Draws process portraits and builds towers
Creativity: Dictates pages for a personal book

printableIdeas.title: All About Me Picture Card Pack (PDF)
printableIdeas.purpose: Inclusive faces, families, interests, and affirmation cards for mirror play, interviews, and dramatic play.

songs.title: I Am Me (LLH Affirmation)
songs.rightsEvidence: Original LLH affirmation chant written for All About Me preschool week.
songs.lyrics:
I am me, you are you,
Different hair and feelings too.
Clap for you and clap for me,
We belong here—1, 2, 3!
songs.motions: Point to self; point to friend; touch hair; heart hands; clap three times.
songs.teacherDirections: Teach seated first. Invite whispered verse for shy voices.
songs.whenToUse: Monday mirror time and Friday celebration.

songs.title: Wiggle What You Will (LLH)
songs.rightsEvidence: Original LLH inclusive movement chant written to replace uncertain rights on familiar classroom body songs. Lyrics and motions authored for Little Learner Hub.
songs.lyrics:
Wiggle what you will today—
Fingers, elbows, wheels that sway.
Freeze like stone, then soft and small,
Move your way—we cheer you all!
songs.motions: Wiggle chosen body part or roll wheels; freeze; curl small; open arms to cheer.
songs.teacherDirections: Offer seated/wheeled options every line. Never spotlight one body as the model.
songs.whenToUse: Tuesday movement game and Thursday warm-up.

songs.title: Friends Wave Hello (LLH)
songs.rightsEvidence: Original LLH greeting/closing chant for All About Me; not adapted from a commercial folk arrangement.
songs.lyrics:
Friends wave hello, hello, hello,
Friends wave hello—we’re glad you came.
Friends wave goodbye, goodbye, goodbye,
Friends wave goodbye—remember my name!
songs.motions: Wave; point around the circle; wave goodbye; point to own name card.
songs.teacherDirections: Use at celebration circle; solitary wave option allowed.
songs.transitionPurpose: Close the week with community language.

books.title: I Like Myself!
books.author: Karen Beaumont
books.verificationSource: Author site karenbeaumont.com/i-like-myself/ and Harcourt/HMH listing ISBN 9780152020132 credit Karen Beaumont (author), David Catrow (illustrator); Publishers Weekly review confirms; ages preschool–grade 2.
books.whyThisBook: Supports mirror and affirmation work without requiring a single body ideal.
beforeReadingQuestions: What is one thing you like about being you?
duringReadingPrompts: How is the character feeling here?
What silly thing do they imagine?
afterReadingQuestions: What should we put in our ‘I am me’ book today?
books.substituteTitle: No book: children complete the sentence ‘I like my…’ with picture cards.

books.title: From Head to Toe
books.author: Eric Carle
books.verificationSource: HarperCollins / standard catalogs credit Eric Carle; movement invitation book commonly used ages 2–5.
books.whyThisBook: Pairs with inclusive movement game; animals invite imitation without ranking children.
beforeReadingQuestions: Which animal move do you want to try?
duringReadingPrompts: Can you move like this animal in your own way?
What body part is working hard?
afterReadingQuestions: Which move should lead our scarf path?
books.substituteTitle: Head, Shoulders chant with adapted motions if the book is unavailable.

books.title: Chrysanthemum
books.author: Kevin Henkes
books.verificationSource: Greenwillow Books / HarperCollins catalogs credit Kevin Henkes; picture book about names and belonging, typical preschool–early elementary read-aloud (teacher paces for preschool).
books.whyThisBook: Centers names and kindness—pairs with name discovery and friend interviews.
beforeReadingQuestions: What do you like about your name?
duringReadingPrompts: How does Chrysanthemum feel at school?
afterReadingQuestions: How can we make sure every name feels welcome here?
books.substituteTitle: I Like Myself! reread focused on names we heard this week.
